Seminar Title:

Effect of Rolling Strain Path on Deformation Behaviour, Microstructure, Crystallographic Texture, and Mechanical Anisotropy of Nb–10Hf–1Ti Refractory Alloy Sheets: Experimental Investigation and Crystal Plasticity Modelling

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Metallurgical and Materials Engineering

Speaker Name:

Yogesh Singh ( Rollno : 521mm1002)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

M. Tech. Classroom, Annex Building, MM Department

Date and Time:

09 Jul 2026 4:00 PM

Contact:

Kumud Kant Mehta

Abstract:

Among refractory alloys, Nb&ndash10Hf&ndash1Ti (commercially known as C-103) has emerged as the most widely used niobium-based refractory alloy particularly in thin-gauge sheet form for aerospace propulsion systems owing to its excellent combination of low density, high-temperature strength, superior ductility, weldability, fabricability, and microstructural stability above 1200 &degC. The thin-gauge sheets are extensively used for manufacturing rocket nozzle extensions, combustion chambers, and spacecraft thruster assemblies. However, as thick-gauge Nb&ndash10Hf&ndash1Ti alloy sheets are progressively cold rolled into thin-gauge sheets, their mechanical performance and formability become increasingly sensitive to the rolling-induced microstructure and crystallographic texture, often resulting in pronounced mechanical anisotropy. Although rolling strain-path modification and post-rolling annealing are expected to strongly influence microstructure, texture evolution, recrystallization behaviour, and plastic anisotropy, their combined effects have not yet been systematically investigated. The present investigation addresses this gap through comprehensive experimental characterization integrated with Visco-Plastic Self-Consistent (VPSC) crystal plasticity modelling. Conventionally processed Nb&ndash10Hf&ndash1Ti alloy sheets produced through the ingot metallurgy route were subjected to unidirectional rolling (UR) and two-step cross rolling (CR) to produce 1 mm thick sheets. The rolled sheets were subsequently vacuum annealed under nine temperature&ndashtime combinations (1100&ndash1250 &degC for 1&ndash3 h) to identify the optimum annealing conditions based on strength&ndashductility synergy. Microstructural characterization was carried out using optical microscopy, FE-SEM, TEM, EBSD, and XRD, while mechanical behaviour was evaluated through room-temperature tensile testing along different orientations with respect to the rolling direction. VPSC simulations were employed to model rolling deformation, tensile behaviour, texture evolution, and slip-system activity. The results demonstrate that the conventionally annealed sheet exhibits pronounced directional dependence of yield strength and work-hardening behaviour because of its strong rolling texture. Cross rolling significantly modified the deformation microstructure by promoting cellular dislocation structures, enhancing multiple slip-system activation, and transforming the dominant &gamma-fibre texture into a stronger &alpha-fibre texture. The modified strain path also accelerated recrystallization during annealing, producing finer and more homogeneous microstructures. Annealing optimization established that 1175 &degC for 2 h (U1175-2) and 1250 &degC for 1 h (C1250-1) provided the optimum strength&ndashductility combinations for UR and CR sheets, respectively. VPSC simulations successfully reproduced the experimental stress&ndashstrain behaviour and demonstrated that the directional variation in tensile strength is governed by the relative activation of the {110}〈111〉, {112}〈111〉, and {123}〈111〉 slip systems. Furthermore, the optimized cross-rolled sheet exhibited substantially reduced ductility anisotropy because of its homogeneous recrystallized microstructure. Overall, this study establishes the processing&ndashmicrostructure&ndashtexture&ndashproperty relationships in Nb&ndash10Hf&ndash1Ti alloy sheets and demonstrates that rolling strain-path modification combined with optimized annealing provides an effective strategy for improving the mechanical performance and reducing plastic anisotropy for advanced aerospace applications.

Keywords: Nb&ndash10Hf&ndash1Ti alloy Rolling strain path Crystallographic texture Plastic anisotropy Recrystallization VPSC modelling.
